summary: Malheur NF summit lookout in Grant County; present R-6 cab moved here from Lake Butte in 1974; register lists 1963 build year that other sources do not support.

facts.design: R-6 flat-top cab with catwalk on a 30-foot pole tower
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Malheur National Forest (Prairie City Ranger District)

events.note: First lookout at the site: a 20-foot tower with an L-4 cab, per the Forest Service archive file. Other sources give 1928 (1961 memo) or 1930 (register, firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill).

R-6 cab and 30-foot tower moved from Lake Butte (about 45 air miles away) to Antelope Mountain under a 1974 Forest Service contract (bid awarded to Emmert Industrial Corp.); the contract called for removing the old tower and house here.

corrections.proposed: 1929 (first lookout at the site); current R-6 cab moved here in 1974
corrections.why: The register's own description places the first lookout in 1930 and the present cab's arrival in 1974. No other source read gives 1963. The Forest Service archive file records a 1929 tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 1928 (1961 inspection note), 1929 (archive file) and 1930 (register, firelookout.com, Cheryl Hill). The story uses 1929 and notes the range.
Register gives a 31-foot tower; firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill say 30 feet. The record keeps 9.1 m (30 feet).
The 1974 contract allowed the contractor to choose how far to dismantle the cab; a 2022 visitor reports it moved intact by truck. Both can be true.

sources.title: Antelope Mountain - Every Lookout in Oregon

notes_for_editor: The build year is disputed (1928/1929/1930) and the register's 1963 is unsupported; the story says so. The 1974 move is well documented by a contract quoted on Forest Lookouts. The record's coordinates match the register; another source in the brief's record gives a point about 470 m away, which was not read. Whether the cab is open to visitors inside is not stated in any source read. The 2022 Cheryl Hill visit is the newest source. The register's 1963 may be a data-entry error; a Malheur NF or NHLR contact could confirm.
